title: Memory MCP Server
summary: Give your agent a persistent knowledge graph of people, projects and decisions that survives between sessions, stored in one local JSONL file.
description: The memory server keeps a graph made of entities, the observations attached to them, and directed relations between them. Tools such as create_entities, add_observations, search_nodes and read_graph let the agent write and recall facts.
Everything lives in a single JSONL file on your disk. Point MEMORY_FILE_PATH at a folder you own, because a file inside the npx cache can be wiped when packages update.
It needs Node.js 24 or later and no account.
useWhen: Remember team conventions from one session to the next
Track which services depend on each other
Keep a running list of decisions and why they were made
Store preferences so you stop repeating them

mcp.name: memory

env.name: MEMORY_FILE_PATH
env.description: Absolute path of the JSONL file that holds the graph; the folder must already exist

access: Reads and rewrites one memory file at the path you set
Can delete entities, relations and observations in that file

example.prompt: Remember that the billing service owns the invoices table and is maintained by the payments team.
example.result: Created entities billing-service and payments-team, added the observation that billing-service owns the invoices table, and linked the two with a maintained_by relation.

faq.question: Where is my data kept?
faq.answer: In the JSONL file named by MEMORY_FILE_PATH. Nothing is sent to a cloud service, and you can open the file in any editor or back it up.

faq.question: Can two agents share it?
faq.answer: Yes, if both use the same file path. Writes take a lock file next to the memory file, so they do not corrupt each other.

faq.question: How do I start over?
faq.answer: Delete or move the JSONL file, or ask the agent to remove entities with delete_entities.

access: Reads and writes the memory file you configure
